tools.name: ls
tools.description: List directory contents. Returns entries sorted alphabetically, with '/' suffix for directories. Output is truncated to 500 entries or 50KB (whichever is hit first).

tools.name: bash
tools.description: Execute a bash command in the working directory; returns stdout and stderr, truncated to the last 2000 lines or 50KB. Timeouts you set are retried automatically (3 attempts total) as [bash attempt N]; environment-default timeouts fail once with the partial output. For long-running commands (builds, servers, watchers) pass background: true — you get the job id immediately and a notice when it finishes; check progress with bash_job. A foreground command still running when the user sends a message is moved to a background job untouched (never killed). A command still running after 60s is moved to a background job automatically (never restarted); carried timeouts are NOT auto-retried — retry if the completion notice reports a timeout. A `cmd &`/nohup survivor of a call is adopted as a tracked job (completion reported; no captured output or exit code).

tools.name: bash_job
tools.description: Manage background shell jobs (from bash background: true, and adopted cmd & / nohup survivors). Actions: "status" lists running + last 20 exited (all: true = every job; id = one), "output" tails a log (id, lines), "stop" kills a running job (id).

tools.name: lsp
tools.description:
Query a language server for diagnostics, navigation, and renames. For Dart/Flutter workspaces the Dart analysis server (`dart language-server`) starts automatically on first use; other servers can be added via `.fah/lsp.json`.

## Ops

- `diagnostics {path}` — analyzer errors/warnings for a file. Returns `OK` when clean.
- `definition {path, line, character}` — where the symbol at the position is defined.
- `references {path, line, character}` — every reference to the symbol at the position.
- `rename {path, line, character, newName}` — rename the symbol at the position workspace-wide. The server's workspace edit is applied atomically, so barrel files and imports update together; per-file edit counts are reported.

`line` and `character` are 1-indexed and default to 1.

## Rules

- Prefer this over `bash dart analyze` for a single file; diagnostics come back scoped and severity-sorted.
- Prefer `rename` over manual search-and-replace for identifiers: the analysis server finds every reference, including exports and imports.
- Positions point at the symbol's first letter. When unsure of the exact column, `read` the line first.
- Definition/references results render as `file:line:col` with the source line; follow up with `read` for more context.
- If no server is configured for a file type, add one to `.fah/lsp.json` (servers map with `command`, `args`, `fileTypes`, `rootMarkers`).

tools.name: web_search
tools.description: Search the web and return ranked results with [n] citation markers, titles, URLs, and snippets. Runs a provider chain (DuckDuckGo first, keyed providers when configured) and falls through on failure. Follow up with web_fetch on a result URL to read the full page.

tools.name: web_fetch
tools.description: Fetch a web page and return its main content as Markdown: headings, link anchors, lists, and code blocks are preserved, navigation and boilerplate are stripped. Known sites (pub.dev) are rendered via dedicated handlers. Use it to read pages found with web_search.

tools.name: memory_add
tools.description:
# `memory_add` policy

## What to store

Store only **durable** facts — things that must survive across sessions:

- project conventions, architecture decisions and their rationale;
- user preferences, habits, environment facts;
- key discoveries that were expensive to learn (non-obvious behaviour,
  gotchas, working configurations).

Do **not** store task progress, transient state, or anything derivable
from the repository itself (file contents, git history, current diffs).

## The supersede rule

Facts age. When a problem is **solved** or a fact **changes**:

1. delete the outdated record (`memory_delete` by id or exact text —
   deletions are tombstoned, so the old text cannot be re-captured);
2. add the new fact as a fresh record.

Never leave temporary difficulties, workarounds, or "currently broken"
notes in memory forever. A memory full of solved problems actively
misleads future sessions. If you used a record to fix something, that
record's job is done — supersede it.

Before adding anything, `memory_search` for an existing record on the
topic: update (delete + add) instead of duplicating.

## Scope discipline

- **project scope** (default) lives in the project's memory directory and
  is **public**: it is committed to git and shared with everyone who
  clones the repository. Never store secrets, credentials, personal data,
  or anything you would not put in a public commit message.
- **user scope** is global and private to the user's machine. Use it for
  cross-project preferences and facts about the user.

## Style

- One fact per record, concise and self-contained (readable without the
  conversation that produced it).
- Add concrete tags (see [tag_taxonomy.md](tag_taxonomy.md)).
- Prefer facts with staying power: "tests run with `--exclude-tags
  integration`" outlives "I am currently fixing the test suite".

tools.name: memory_search
tools.description: Search long-term memory for relevant facts, preferences, or past decisions. Use proactively before tasks that might benefit from prior context.

tools.name: reply
tools.description:
Deliver your explicit answer to the parent agent. Call this when your task output is ready — the text becomes the parent-visible reply. If you never call it, the parent still sees your final message as a completion notice, but an explicit reply is the reliable channel.

REPORT SIZE: per-message budget 8000 chars — you may send one complete reply even when it is larger: the harness auto-spills it (the full text is stored as an agent:// artifact; the parent gets an excerpt + pointer + completeness, and this tool result names the reference). Manual chunking (ordered agent_message parts with report_id + 0-based part_index, more=false on the last, then a final manifest reply carrying report_id + report_parts) is the FALLBACK for when auto-spill is unavailable. See REPORT SIZE CONTRACT in your system prompt. Never probe the output limit.

tools.name: session_search
tools.description: Search the WHOLE session archive (every past turn — hidden, compacted and checkpointed regions included), not just the current context. Use it whenever the user references a past decision, rule, task or artifact ("remember when…", "the rules we made") BEFORE answering from assumption. Returns pointers (id, kind, timestamp, preview), never full content — pull the record back with compact_expand. With mode: "map" it reports the archive structure instead: record-kind counts, hidden/checkpoint totals, checkpoint tree with nesting depth.

# Review Policy

Preset: `default` — resolved from: built-in default (resolution chain: projectConfig.reviewPolicy → workflow jobParams → built-in default).
Verification: `none` — findings post exactly as the review leg raised them — no second-stage verification.
Every verdict on this PR is traceable to this table.

| Severity | Round | Fix | Gates approval |
|---|---|---|---|
| 🚨 BLOCKING | rework | mandatory | YES |
| ⚠️ IMPORTANT | rework | mandatory | YES |
| 💡 SUGGESTION | polish | mandatory | no |
| 🪶 NIT | none | opportunistic | no |

Verification: `none` — findings post exactly as the review leg raised them — no second-stage verification.

Bounds: polishMaxThreads=6 · polishMaxChangedLines=80 · opportunisticMaxThreads=8 · opportunisticSameFilesOnly=true · densityMin=2 · densityMax=8 · sweepBatch=10 · sweepMaxAgeDays=30

Density cap (💡/🪶 threads only; 🚨/⚠️ never capped): allowed = clamp(round(2 + 3*sqrt(additions/200)), 2, 8).
Rank your findings and post the top-K as threads; the overflow becomes a ranked digest list in the general comment. The census counts posted threads + digest lines.

Machine enforcement: the approval is recomputed from the severity census + this policy — the model verdict is advisory. Any 🚨 or ⚠️ open → REQUEST_CHANGES; only 💡/🪶 → APPROVE.
## Downgrade protocol

A rework lap may downgrade a specific ⚠️ IMPORTANT finding to 💡 SUGGESTION **only with a written justification** in the census (the thread reply and the response summary: why this is not maintainability debt). A silent downgrade does not exist: the next review round re-raises it as ⚠️ IMPORTANT and the cycle repeats. A justified downgrade lets a false-⚠️ review converge to APPROVE without a code change.=====

name: JS engine integration (quickjs-ng)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, quality-gate]
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips this leg — the release-pending pre-check decides.
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 25
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@2286a0c042b44434fe26d292bbce8d34f7ec662b # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      - uses: ./.github/actions/sqlite3-native-assets-prewarm
      - name: Install quickjs-ng
        run: |
          curl -fsSL -o "$RUNNER_TEMP/qjs" \
            https://github.com/quickjs-ng/quickjs/releases/download/v0.16.2/qjs-linux-x86_64
          chmod +x "$RUNNER_TEMP/qjs"
          echo "$RUNNER_TEMP" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
      - name: dart test --tags integration (qjs engine suites)
        run: dart test --tags integration test/cli/ext_engine_process_test.dart test/js_ext/integration/

  publish:
    name: Publish to pub.dev
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [quality-gate, integration]
    # 20m ceiling: publish flow (~2-4m) + the post-upload verify window
    # (11m, #611) must both fit — 10m would kill a healthy poll mid-window.
    timeout-minutes: 20
    # !cancelled() + explicit gate check — the fa#456 class: GitHub propagates
    # "skipped" TRANSITIVELY through the always()-quality-gate's needs graph.
    #
    # #1368, two changes:
    # 1. PUSH-EVENT TAGS ONLY. pub.dev trusted publishing accepts OIDC tokens
    #    from push and workflow_dispatch events ONLY — there is no
    #    release-event option (owner verified the pub.dev console). The old
    #    release arm made the release-event twin of every tag ATTEMPT the
    #    publish whenever the push twin had not uploaded — pub.dev rejected
    #    the token's event claim and the leg died "Authentication failed!"
    #    (exit 65) on every release since the gate graph grew legs that can
    #    redden the push twin. The v0.1.370-402 era this arm once covered
    #    (API-created lightweight tags with no push event) is gone: every tag
    #    is PAT-pushed annotated (gh-1522: the auto_release.sh App-token tag
    #    push), so the push twin
    #    always exists. A release-only tag would now skip publish and the
    #    daily verifyPubDev leg alarms «only release-event run(s)» loudly.
    # 2. The gate is dart_ok — the pure-Dart package verdict quality-gate
    #    exports — NOT the aggregate result. A red native binary/PTY leg must
    #    never hold a Dart package hostage (v1.0.520's push twin: publish
    #    skipped off a red pty-integration shard). The Provider smoke stays a
    #    hard gate (#551): needs.integration.result == 'success'.
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.quality-gate.outputs.dart_ok == 'true' &&
      needs.integration.result == 'success' &&
      github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')
    concurrency:
      # push + release events both fire for PAT-pushed tags; serialize the
      # double-fire so the loser no-ops on the already-published guard below
      # instead of racing dart pub publish (version already exists → red).
      # #1368: only the push twin can publish now — the group stays as a
      # belt-and-suspenders guard for re-pushed tags.
      group: publish-${{ github.ref }}
      cancel-in-progress: false
    permissions:
      id-token: write # OIDC — pub.dev verifies the GitHub identity, no secrets
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ╔═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
# ║  SHARED FAST GATE — DO NOT LOWER THESE THRESHOLDS WITHOUT TEAM APPROVAL   ║
# ║  loc ≤ 2800 lines (crap4dart) · analyze · tests · coverage ≥ 80% ·        ║
# ║  duplication < 1% (flutter_app < 3.7%) · cross-module < 0.31%             ║
# ╚═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
#
# THE shared fast gate used by BOTH the pre-commit hook and CI (issue #177,
# AC7). Both callers run this exact script and diff the one-line markers
#   GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP <reason>
# for hook/CI parity. Every known stage ALWAYS prints exactly one marker:
# OK when it ran and passed, SKIP <reason> when it was not selected or a
# required tool is missing. A failing stage aborts the script with exit 1
# BEFORE its OK marker is printed (marker absent = failed).
#
# Usage:
#   scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh [--scope auto|all|core|app|docs] [--stages list] [--hook]
#
#   --scope auto  Derive the scope from changed paths (default):
#                 - in a git hook (--hook flag or GIT_INDEX_FILE set):
#                   staged files via `git diff --cached --name-only`;
#                 - in CI (BASE_REF + HEAD_REF env vars set):
#                   `git diff --name-only $BASE_REF...$HEAD_REF`;
#                 - otherwise: "all" (safe default).
#   --scope all   Run every stage.
#   --scope core  analyze + test-core + coverage + crap + dup + dupx
#                 (hook mode: WITHOUT coverage — the coverage ratchet is
#                 CI-only there, owner directive PR #2435; `--stages
#                 coverage` still runs it standalone).
#   --scope app   analyze + dup + dupx + flutter.
#   --scope docs  analyze only.
#   --stages l    Comma-separated stage list; overrides the scope-derived set.
#                 Known stages: analyze,test-core,coverage,crap,dup,dupx,flutter,integration-mock
#
#
# Path rules (union logic, E1; test/** counts as core, E6):
#   docs/ | *.md | prompts/ .................. analyze
#   lib/ | bin/ | test/ | pubspec.* .......... + test-core, coverage, crap,
#                                              dup, dupx (hook mode: no
#                                              coverage, see --scope core)
#   test/integration/** ...................... + integration-mock (no-key legs,
#                                              MockLlmServer; issue #551)
#   flutter_app/ | packages/ ................. + dup, dupx, flutter
#   scripts/ | .github/ | crap4dart.yaml ..... ALL stages (safe default, E2)
#   anything unknown ......................... ALL stages (safe default)
#
# Concurrency overrides: FA_DART_TEST_CONCURRENCY / FA_FLUTTER_TEST_CONCURRENCY
# (auto-throttled via detect_test_concurrency, same as scripts/pre-commit).
# Flake budget (gh-1026): FA_GATE_PTY_RETRIES=N makes the integration-mock
# stage rerun ONLY its failed files, up to N times, before failing — the
# load-sensitive PTY/grid timing legs stop costing a full 2.5 h leg per
# ambient flake (default 0 = single-shot, behaviour unchanged).
#
# CRAP ratchet scoping: in --hook mode the analyze runs over the STAGED
# lib/bin files only — the ratchet guards what a commit touches, so a
# pre-existing offender in an untouched file cannot block an unrelated
# commit. Non-hook runs (and ci.yml's whole-repo `crap4dart analyze`)
# keep the full-repo view, so nothing escapes the ratchet permanently.

      - name: Root allow-list guard (gh-2185)
        run: |
          python3 scripts/check_root_allowlist.py --self-test

      # Issue #1234: the ≤2800-line file guard MOVED into crap4dart's loc
      # gate (crap4dart.yaml, wc -l parity verified by the maintainer

      # `crap4dart check --baseline` Quality-gates step below. The shell
      # find-exec guard (gh-1232 AC2) is gone: one enforcement point, no
      # drifted exclusions.

      # Issue #1100: the fa-web-spa.zip packaging guard (base-tag patch +
      # absolute-/app/ grep) must stay functional on every PR — a release
      # run is the wrong place to first discover a broken guard. Fixture
      # self-test: positive path + all red exits, pure bash, no web build.
      - uses: ./.github/actions/sqlite3-native-assets-prewarm
      - name: Web SPA packaging guard self-test (#1100)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          d=$(mktemp -d)
          trap 'rm -rf "$d"' EXIT
          mkdir -p "$d/build"
          printf '<html><head>\n<base href="/app/">\n</head></html>\n' > "$d/build/index.html"

# fa self-configuration

You are reconfiguring fa itself. The config file IS the source of truth: the
CLI settings commands (`/provider`, `/tools`, `/approval`, …) are thin
editors over the same YAML this skill edits. Edit the file, never invent
keys, verify after every edit, and report what changed and when it applies.

## Hard rules

1. **Never invent keys.** Unknown top-level keys are ignored silently; strict
   sections throw `ConfigException` on unknown keys or bad value types and can
   break startup — `mcp:`, `memory:`, `cube:`, `providerTimeouts:`, `skills:`,
   `images:`, `models.custom` fields, `ttsr:`. The `tools:` section throws on
   non-boolean values; unknown TOOL ids only warn (and absent capabilities can
   never be force-enabled). Every key you write must come from this document.
2. **Never write API key VALUES into config.yaml.** Config carries key NAMES
   (`apiKeyName:`) only. Values live in the OS secure store (`/key set`) or the
   environment. A key value in YAML is a leaked secret.
3. **Preserve the file.** Edit surgically (the `edit` tool, or `write` only for
   a file you fully own). Keep comments and unrelated keys byte-identical.
4. **Verify after every edit.** Run the `config` tool's `check` op (or
   `fa config check`) and confirm it passes before declaring success. A
   broken file must be detected by you, not discovered at next boot.
5. **Report scope + application.** Every change report states: which file, which
   scope, and whether it applies live or at next boot.

## Config layout and precedence

| File | Scope | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `~/.fah/config.yaml` | user (global) | main settings file; loaded by `loadCliConfig` |
| `<project>/.fah/config.yaml` | project | only the `memory:`, `cube:`, `tools:`, `spills:` sections and the `agent.contextWindowCap` key are read from here — each wins over the user file |
| `<project>/.fah/rules.yaml` | project | TTSR stream rules; project rules win name clashes over the `ttsr:` section |
| `<project>/.fah/lsp.json` | project | LSP server map |
| `<project>/.fah/packages.yaml` | project | plugin configuration |
| `~/.dap/config.json` | user | DAP hub identity/channels (written by the `/settings` hub flow, not YAML) |

Project precedence is per section, not per file: `memory:`, `cube:`,
`tools:` and `spills:` are loaded separately from the project file
(`loadProjectMemoryConfig`, `loadProjectCubeSettings`,
`loadProjectToolsConfig`, `loadProjectSpillsConfig`) and win over the
same section in `~/.fah/config.yaml`. All other sections are read from
the user file only — with ONE exception: `agent.contextWindowCap` is
also read from the project file (`loadProjectContextWindowCap`; the
project value wins over the user value, and the boot log line
`context window cap source=project window=<n>` names the winner). Every
other `agent.*` key in a project file is dead config (`fa config check`
names it).

Project sections are strict: a present-but-invalid section throws
`ConfigException` at startup. A project `.fah/` that does not exist yet is
created with a minimal valid file — never leave a half-written YAML behind
(write to a temp name and rename, or write the full content in one `write`).

## Workflow

1. Read the request; identify the topic section below.
2. Inspect current state: `config` op `get <key>` / `path` (or read the two
   config files — a missing file means defaults, not an error).
3. Make the edit: `config` op `set` (preferred — it validates before
   writing and preserves the rest of the file byte-for-byte). Fall back to
   a surgical file edit (rule 3) only for what `set` cannot express:
   removing a key.
4. Verify: `config` op `check` (rule 4).
5. Report (rule 5), naming the CLI command equivalent that would have made
   the same change.

## The config tool

The primary editing surface on every host — CLI, desktop app, web, iOS —
because it needs no shell and no `fa` process. One tool, four ops over the
same core the human CLI verbs wrap:

| op | args | effect |
|---|---|---|
| `check` | — | validate both config files with the real parsers; prints errors, warnings, notes and a final `config check: ok` / `config check: failed` |
| `path` | — | list the config file locations and whether each exists |
| `get` | `key` | the effective value of a dotted key; project scope wins for `memory`/`cube`/`tools`/`spills` and `agent.contextWindowCap` |
| `set` | `key`, `value`, `scope`? | surgical single-key write; the edited file is validated BEFORE the write, so an invalid value persists nothing |

`set` answers with the file, scope, old → new value, and whether the change
applies live or at next boot — echo that in your report (rule 5). `scope`
defaults by key: `memory`/`cube`/`tools` → the project file (created minimal
when absent), everything else → the user file; pass `global` or `project`
to override. Keys come from the topic sections below — the tool rejects
unknown top-level keys instead of writing them.
`set` also takes LIST-VALUED keys: pass the value as compact JSON (an
array or object) and it is rendered as a yaml block — `customProviders`
provider entries are settable this way, e.g. `config` op `set`, key
`customProviders`, value
`[{"name":"my-llama","apiType":"openai","baseUrl":"http://localhost:11434/v1","modelId":"llama3"}]`.
`get` reports list-valued keys as the same compact JSON, so the round
trip is get → edit the JSON → set. A whole list is replaced; to add one
entry, get first and re-set the extended list.
`get` of a platform-inapplicable key and `set` of one answer
`not applicable on this host` with the reason — never write there and
never suggest a file edit as a workaround. The stdio members of an MCP
server (`command`/`args`/`env`) need host process spawning: on web and
iOS/Android containers they are refused; configure a remote server via
`mcp.servers.<id>.url` instead. On a host with no home directory (web)
the global scope is refused for every user-file key — only the project
sections (`memory`/`cube`/`tools`) persist there.

Human/script equivalent (thin wrappers over the same service):
`fa config check`, `fa config path`, `fa config get <dotted.key>`,
`fa config set <dotted.key> <value> [--project|--global]`, and
`fa config export-providers [--out <file.fahx>]` (provider-preset export —
the one verb without a config-file write).

## Verification

`config` op `check` (or `fa config check`) validates both files with the
REAL section parsers and prints named diagnostics — this is the mandatory
final step of every edit:

- **What check reports as errors** (non-zero exit / `config check: failed`):
  yaml syntax errors, strict-section schema errors (`mcp:`, `memory:`,
  `cube:`, `tools:`, `providerTimeouts:`, `skills:`, `images:`, `roles:`,
  `ttsr:`, `models.custom`, `fabric:`), and bad scalar types — each naming
  file+section.
- **Warnings**: unknown top-level keys (the runtime silently ignores them;
  the check does not — a typo must not survive) and dead project-file keys.
- **At next boot, semantic errors in strict sections are FATAL**:
  `invalid ~/.fah/config.yaml: <named diagnostic>` — the process refuses to
  start rather than boot a broken config. A passing check is what stands
  between your edit and that.
- **YAML syntax errors remain silent at RUNTIME** (an unparseable file falls
  back to defaults) — `check` is the only place they are reported, which is
  why it is mandatory.
- **Live re-read surfaces**: in a running REPL, `/tools reload` and
  `/mcp reload` re-read their sections immediately and print the parse
  error instead of applying it — use them as the live check when a REPL
  exists.
- Runtime objects keep the last good config when a reload fails (the failed
  section never half-applies), so a loud reload error means "nothing changed".

## Provider & keys

<!-- parity: /provider /providers -->

User file, top-level keys:

```yaml
provider: openai-completions   # openai-completions | anthropic | google | dial | minimax | zai
model: openai/gpt-4o-mini      # model id sent to the provider
baseUrl: https://openrouter.ai/api/v1
```

Saved custom endpoints (the `/provider custom` flow persists here):

```yaml
customProviders:
  - name: my-llama             # non-empty, unique
    apiType: openai            # openai | anthropic | google | dial | openrouter
    baseUrl: http://localhost:11434/v1
    modelId: llama3            # non-empty
    keyName: MY_KEY            # optional: env/secure-store NAME, never the value
    authMethod: apiKey         # apiKey | sso | jwt (optional)
```

Applies: a direct YAML edit takes effect at next boot. `/provider <name>
[baseUrl] [token]` switches the live session too.
Keys: never inline values (rule 2). Key resolution order — environment value,
then endpoint-scoped secure-store entry (`FA_KEY_<HOST>`), then legacy env-name
store entries. `/key set|delete` manages the store and has NO config.yaml
equivalent — that is deliberate.

Scoped provider timeouts (issue #1554): `connectTimeoutMs`/`streamIdleTimeoutMs`
are valid on `roles:` chain entries, `customProviders:` entries, and

wins — **role chain entry > customProviders entry > models.custom entry >

hard sanity bound 1 h). Configs without the keys behave byte-identically.

only `streamIdleTimeoutMs` ≈ 2× the model's worst silent prefill stretch —
the cloud providers in the same config keep the global watchdog untouched,
and the stall line names the override (`idle window 1800s (role default
override)`) so a wide window never reads as a hang.

Media slot names (exact): `imageGeneration`, `audioTts`, `musicGeneration`,
`videoGeneration`, `vision`, `transcription`. A slot without an override is
UNCONFIGURED — media calls fail with an actionable "configure the slot"
error; the main connection serves a slot only through the explicit
`useMainConnection: true` opt-in, and `unsupported: true` removes the
capability entirely (media tools refuse the slot, the pickers drop it from
capability hints).

The `images:` section has no settings-hub editor — the registry is runtime
state, not a persisted setting: `/images` (CLI) and the app's image-drop

notice model is latched (one notice per meaningful change, issue #1889;
see `docs/images.md`). The three keys above are the whole config surface,
applied at next boot.

`/models config` displays this section, `/models set <slot> <model>

yaml. CLI equivalent: `/providers queue list|add|remove|move|test`;

## Power

User file section (issue #325, reworked in #326). Sleep prevention for
live runs — by default ONE assertion PER RUN (acquired when the run
goes in flight, released when it settles), so the machine cannot
idle/sleep out from under a long run but CAN sleep while the agent
idles between turns:

```yaml
power:
  sleepPrevention: idle # off | idle | display | system (default idle)
  hold: per-run # per-run | session (default per-run)
```

Levels are cumulative: `idle` keeps the system from idle-sleeping
(macOS `caffeinate -i`), `display` also keeps the display awake
(`-i -d`), `system` also blocks AC system sleep and declares the user
active (`-i -d -s -u`). `hold: session` is the explicit opt-in that
holds from session start to exit instead (always-on deployments).
macOS spawns `caffeinate -w <fa pid>` (exits with fa — never
orphaned), Linux tries `systemd-inhibit` best-effort, other platforms
no-op. A failed assertion is a warning, never a crash.

CLI equivalent: `/power` (level + hold + held state). Applies at next
boot.

## Subagents heartbeat

User file section (issue #383). While a background subagent runs, the
parent receives a periodic status digest through the steering channel —
age, provider requests/tokens, last activity, and a
`healthy | stalled | no-progress-since-spawn` classification per running
child. A child with no provider activity for `stallMinutes` (or that
never issued a request at all) gets a loud `⚠ STALLED` flag with the
suggested `task_status → task_cancel → respawn` action; the flag
escalates to `⚠⚠` at twice the threshold:

```yaml
subagents:
  heartbeatMinutes: 10 # digests cadence; 0 disables the heartbeat
  stallMinutes: 20 # quiet window before a stall flag; 0 disables flags
  replyAutoSpill: true # oversized child replies auto-spill to an artifact
```

Zero running children → no digest; completion notices are unchanged.
Config changes apply at the next digest tick — no restart required.

`subagents.replyAutoSpill` (gh-1956, default `true`): an oversized child
`reply` spills to an artifact automatically — the parent receives a bounded
excerpt + `agent://` pointer + completeness marker instead of raw bytes, and
manual chunking degrades to a fallback. Set it to `false` to restore the
pure-chunk behavior (the child must chunk long reports manually).

## Theme

<!-- parity: /theme -->

The TUI palette is data, never code. `/theme` lists every available theme
(built-ins first, then user themes) with a swatch preview; `/theme <name>`
switches immediately and persists the choice; `/theme reset` returns to
the default.

Config equivalent — the persisted theme name:

```yaml
tui:
  theme: default   # a built-in name or a user theme file stem
```

Built-in names: `default` (the historical site palette — teal `#5eead4`,
indigo `#818cf8`), `catppuccin`, `nord`, `dracula`, `ohmypi-dark`,
`ohmypi-light`, `pi`.

User themes live in `~/.fah/themes/<name>.json`; the file stem is the
theme name, and a user theme can never shadow a built-in (a clashing file
name is skipped with a boot note). The JSON holds a `"roles"` object mapping ROLE names to hex colors
(`"#rgb"` or `"#rrggbb"`): `accent`, `accent2`, `muted`, `highlight`,
`success`, `warning`, `error`, `border`, `focusBorder`, `userMessageBg`.
Every role is optional — a missing role inherits the default theme for
that slot. Unknown role names, invalid hex, or broken JSON produce a
named error (file, role, line) at load time, never a crash.

Applies: `/theme <name>` switches the live session in one frame; a direct
YAML edit takes effect at next boot. Asked to create a theme from a
description, write the JSON file, then apply it with `/theme <name>` and
confirm the swatch line with the user. Asked for a palette "like X" where
X is unknown, ask two or three palette questions first — never invent one
silently.

By default an auto-compaction fold prints ONE short marker line
(`● auto-compacted · engine: N → M tokens (F freed · P%)`); the internal
checkpoint summary stays in the session file (reachable via
`compact_expand`) and out of the console. To render the full report block
(records + fenced summary) and the live summarizer stream on headless
runs, opt in:

```yaml
tui:
  showCompactionDetails: true
```

The manual `/compact` command always renders the full block. Applies at
next boot.

## Output

<!-- parity: none (boot config only) -->

Console-output behavior flags (gh-1198 + gh-1433), user file. Today one
key — the live thinking stream for CLI line-mode runs: with
`streamThinking: true` (or the `--stream-thinking` flag, which wins for

Since gh-1433 this key decides the INTERACTIVE faces only: a headless

flags needed). `--no-stream-thinking` silences thinking for one headless
run (the reasoning liveness line returns), and `FA_LOG_FIDELITY=legacy`
reverts the whole headless face to the pre-gh-1433 byte shape for edge
hosts that parse the log. Rendered deltas — thinking AND streamed text,
on every face — pass through the redaction pipeline at render time since
gh-1433: a registered secret echoed in a delta is masked live, so
byte-pin tests for interactive `--stream-thinking` sessions must assume
redacted deltas whenever redaction is enabled (default).

```yaml

```

tool-result spilling only, `userThreshold: 0` the user path only:

```yaml
spills:
  enabled: true # kill switch; false = byte-identical legacy
  threshold: 8192 # chars above which a tool result spills; 0 = tools off
  headChars: 2000 # preview head bound (chars)
  tailChars: 2000 # preview tail bound (chars)
  userThreshold: 16384 # absolute byte floor for the user path; 0 = user off
  userFraction: 0.5 # spill a user message over this fraction of the live window budget
```

Applies at next boot.

## Session retention

<!-- parity: none (boot config only) -->

The `sessions:` section (gh-1746) is the opt-in disk hygiene policy for
the sessions root: when the total on disk crosses `maxTotalBytes`, a
boot sweep deletes whole session units oldest-last-used-first. Live
sessions (fresh heartbeats), named sessions, and sessions younger than
`minAgeDays` are always exempt — and with no `sessions:` section at all
nothing is EVER auto-deleted (byte-identical legacy boot). Tolerant
parse: unknown keys become notes, never boot failures. Run
`fa session clean [--dry-run]` to enforce the policy manually;
`sweep: off` makes the manual verb the only enforcement path:

```yaml
sessions:
  retention:
    maxTotalBytes: 5368709120 # total cap in bytes (0 = no cap, default)
    minAgeDays: 14 # never delete sessions used more recently than this
    keepNamed: true # named sessions (fa --session <name>) are exempt
    sweep: boot # boot (sweep at startup) | off (manual `fa session clean` only)
```

Applies at next boot (the sweep runs before the session opens).

lib/src/prompts/prompts.g.dart:369:      '---
name: self-settings
description: >
  Configure fa (flutter_agent_harness) itself by editing the exact config
  files the CLI settings commands write: provider/model selection and roles,
  memory paths, tool availability, cubes, MCP servers, redaction, skills
  access, approval and mode, themes and TUI appearance (tui.theme: switch
  or create a theme). Use when asked to reconfigure fa without a human
  in the REPL ("switch us to provider X", "point project memory at this
  path", "disable web_search for this project", "switch the theme to
  ohmypi").
when_to_use: Reconfiguring fa itself — settings, provider, models, memory,
  tools, cubes, MCP, redaction, skills access, themes/TUI appearance — on
  any host (CLI headless, REPL, app), by editing the YAML config the CLI
  persists (themes also via ~/.fah/themes/*.json), never by guessing keys.
argument-hint: "[what to configure, e.g. 'point project memory at ./memory']"
allowed-tools:
  - read
  - write
  - edit
  - ls
  - bash
  - config
user-invocable: true
disable-model-invocation: false
---

# fa self-configuration

You are reconfiguring fa itself. The config file IS the source of truth: the
CLI settings commands (`/provider`, `/tools`, `/approval`, …) are thin
editors over the same YAML this skill edits. Edit the file, never invent
keys, verify after every edit, and report what changed and when it applies.

## Hard rules

1. **Never invent keys.** Unknown top-level keys are ignored silently; strict
   sections throw `ConfigException` on unknown keys or bad value types and can
   break startup — `mcp:`, `memory:`, `cube:`, `providerTimeouts:`, `skills:`,
   `images:`, `models.custom` fields, `ttsr:`. The `tools:` section throws on
   non-boolean values; unknown TOOL ids only warn (and absent capabilities can
   never be force-enabled). Every key you write must come from this document.
2. **Never write API key VALUES into config.yaml.** Config carries key NAMES
   (`apiKeyName:`) only. Values live in the OS secure store (`/key set`) or the
   environment. A key value in YAML is a leaked secret.
3. **Preserve the file.** Edit surgically (the `edit` tool, or `write` only for
   a file you fully own). Keep comments and unrelated keys byte-identical.
4. **Verify after every edit.** Run the `config` tool's `check` op (or
   `fa config check`) and confirm it passes before declaring success. A
   broken file must be detected by you, not discovered at next boot.
5. **Report scope + application.** Every change report states: which file, which
   scope, and whether it applies live or at next boot.

## Config layout and precedence

| File | Scope | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `~/.fah/config.yaml` | user (global) | main settings file; loaded by `loadCliConfig` |
| `<project>/.fah/config.yaml` | project | only the `memory:`, `cube:`, `tools:`, `spills:` sections and the `agent.contextWindowCap` key are read from here — each wins over the user file |
| `<project>/.fah/rules.yaml` | project | TTSR stream rules; project rules win name clashes over the `ttsr:` section |
| `<project>/.fah/lsp.json` | project | LSP server map |
| `<project>/.fah/packages.yaml` | project | plugin configuration |
| `~/.dap/config.json` | user | DAP hub identity/channels (written by the `/settings` hub flow, not YAML) |

Project precedence is per section, not per file: `memory:`, `cube:`,
`tools:` and `spills:` are loaded separately from the project file
(`loadProjectMemoryConfig`, `loadProjectCubeSettings`,
`loadProjectToolsConfig`, `loadProjectSpillsConfig`) and win over the
same section in `~/.fah/config.yaml`. All other sections are read from
the user file only — with ONE exception: `agent.contextWindowCap` is
also read from the project file (`loadProjectContextWindowCap`; the
project value wins over the user value, and the boot log line
`context window cap source=project window=<n>` names the winner). Every
other `agent.*` key in a project file is dead config (`fa config check`
names it).

Project sections are strict: a present-but-invalid section throws
`ConfigException` at startup. A project `.fah/` that does not exist yet is
created with a minimal valid file — never leave a half-written YAML behind
(write to a temp name and rename, or write the full content in one `write`).

## Workflow

1. Read the request; identify the topic section below.
2. Inspect current state: `config` op `get <key>` / `path` (or read the two
   config files — a missing file means defaults, not an error).
3. Make the edit: `config` op `set` (preferred — it validates before
   writing and preserves the rest of the file byte-for-byte). Fall back to
   a surgical file edit (rule 3) only for what `set` cannot express:
   removing a key.
4. Verify: `config` op `check` (rule 4).
5. Report (rule 5), naming the CLI command equivalent that would have made
   the same change.

## The config tool

The primary editing surface on every host — CLI, desktop app, web, iOS —
because it needs no shell and no `fa` process. One tool, four ops over the
same core the human CLI verbs wrap:

| op | args | effect |
|---|---|---|
| `check` | — | validate both config files with the real parsers; prints errors, warnings, notes and a final `config check: ok` / `config check: failed` |
| `path` | — | list the config file locations and whether each exists |
| `get` | `key` | the effective value of a dotted key; project scope wins for `memory`/`cube`/`tools`/`spills` and `agent.contextWindowCap` |
| `set` | `key`, `value`, `scope`? | surgical single-key write; the edited file is validated BEFORE the write, so an invalid value persists nothing |

`set` answers with the file, scope, old → new value, and whether the change
applies live or at next boot — echo that in your report (rule 5). `scope`
defaults by key: `memory`/`cube`/`tools` → the project file (created minimal
when absent), everything else → the user file; pass `global` or `project`
to override. Keys come from the topic sections below — the tool rejects
unknown top-level keys instead of writing them.
`set` also takes LIST-VALUED keys: pass the value as compact JSON (an
array or object) and it is rendered as a yaml block — `customProviders`
provider entries are settable this way, e.g. `config` op `set`, key
`customProviders`, value
`[{"name":"my-llama","apiType":"openai","baseUrl":"http://localhost:11434/v1","modelId":"llama3"}]`.
`get` reports list-valued keys as the same compact JSON, so the round
trip is get → edit the JSON → set. A whole list is replaced; to add one
entry, get first and re-set the extended list.
`get` of a platform-inapplicable key and `set` of one answer
`not applicable on this host` with the reason — never write there and
never suggest a file edit as a workaround. The stdio members of an MCP
server (`command`/`args`/`env`) need host process spawning: on web and
iOS/Android containers they are refused; configure a remote server via
`mcp.servers.<id>.url` instead. On a host with no home directory (web)
the global scope is refused for every user-file key — only the project
sections (`memory`/`cube`/`tools`) persist there.

Human/script equivalent (thin wrappers over the same service):
`fa config check`, `fa config path`, `fa config get <dotted.key>`,
`fa config set <dotted.key> <value> [--project|--global]`, and
`fa config export-providers [--out <file.fahx>]` (provider-preset export —
the one verb without a config-file write).

## Verification

`config` op `check` (or `fa config check`) validates both files with the
REAL section parsers and prints named diagnostics — this is the mandatory
final step of every edit:

- **What check reports as errors** (non-zero exit / `config check: failed`):
  yaml syntax errors, strict-section schema errors (`mcp:`, `memory:`,
  `cube:`, `tools:`, `providerTimeouts:`, `skills:`, `images:`, `roles:`,
  `ttsr:`, `models.custom`, `fabric:`), and bad scalar types — each naming
  file+section.
- **Warnings**: unknown top-level keys (the runtime silently ignores them;
  the check does not — a typo must not survive) and dead project-file keys.
- **At next boot, semantic errors in strict sections are FATAL**:
  `invalid ~/.fah/config.yaml: <named diagnostic>` — the process refuses to
  start rather than boot a broken config. A passing check is what stands
  between your edit and that.
- **YAML syntax errors remain silent at RUNTIME** (an unparseable file falls
  back to defaults) — `check` is the only place they are reported, which is
  why it is mandatory.
- **Live re-read surfaces**: in a running REPL, `/tools reload` and
  `/mcp reload` re-read their sections immediately and print the parse
  error instead of applying it — use them as the live check when a REPL
  exists.
- Runtime objects keep the last good config when a reload fails (the failed
  section never half-applies), so a loud reload error means "nothing changed".

## CLI parity map

Every settings command below has a config-file equivalent documented in this
skill. If a new settings command appears in the CLI without a section here,
this skill has rotted — flag it in your report.

| CLI | Section |
|---|---|
| `/provider`, `/providers` | [Provider & keys](#provider--keys) |
| `/model`, `/models`, `/model-edit` | [Models & roles](#models--roles) |
| `/memory` | [Memory](#memory) |
| `/tools` | [Tool availability](#tool-availability) |
| `/cube` | [Cubes](#cubes) |
| `/mcp` | [MCP servers](#mcp-servers) |
| `/redact` | [Redaction](#redaction) |
| `/skills` | [Skills access](#skills-access) |
| `/approval`, `/allow` | [Approval](#approval) |
| `/mode`, `/code`, `/architect`, `/review` | [Mode](#mode) |
| `/theme` | [Theme](#theme) |
| `/settings` | [Settings hub](#settings-hub) |

<!-- parity: /provider /providers /model /models /model-edit /memory /tools /cube /mcp /redact /skills /approval /allow /mode /code /architect /review /theme /settings -->

The `fa config check|path|get|set` verbs and the `config` tool share their
config-file equivalent with the topic sections above (see
[The config tool](#the-config-tool)); the parity test pins every verb
alongside the slash commands.

## Provider & keys

<!-- parity: /provider /providers -->

User file, top-level keys:

```yaml
provider: openai-completions   # openai-completions | anthropic | google | dial | minimax | zai
model: openai/gpt-4o-mini      # model id sent to the provider
baseUrl: https://openrouter.ai/api/v1
```

Saved custom endpoints (the `/provider custom` flow persists here):

```yaml
customProviders:
  - name: my-llama             # non-empty, unique
    apiType: openai            # openai | anthropic | google | dial | openrouter
    baseUrl: http://localhost:11434/v1
    modelId: llama3            # non-empty
    keyName: MY_KEY            # optional: env/secure-store NAME, never the value
    authMethod: apiKey         # apiKey | sso | jwt (optional)
```

Applies: a direct YAML edit takes effect at next boot. `/provider <name>
[baseUrl] [token]` switches the live session too.
Keys: never inline values (rule 2). Key resolution order — environment value,
then endpoint-scoped secure-store entry (`FA_KEY_<HOST>`), then legacy env-name
store entries. `/key set|delete` manages the store and has NO config.yaml
equivalent — that is deliberate.

<!-- parity: /model /models /model-edit -->

sections:

```yaml
roles:                         # intent → ordered fallback chain
  default:
    - openrouter/anthropic/claude-sonnet-4
    - provider: openai         # or a map entry:
      model: gpt-4o
      apiKeyName: OPENAI_API_KEY   # optional; also baseUrl, contextWindow, maxTokens
      connectTimeoutMs: 45000       # optional per-entry watchdog override

      thinkingLevel: high       # optional: minimal|low|medium|high|xhigh|max

  streamIdleTimeoutMs: 300000

  foregroundCallBudgetSeconds: 600  # foreground tool-call budget B in seconds;

  registry: true               # kill switch — false = byte-for-byte legacy
  maxPerRequest: 20            # per-request unique-image cap (default 20)

      baseUrl: https://api.aiin.by/v1    # minimax, zai, a saved custom…)

wins — **role chain entry > customProviders entry > models.custom entry >

hard sanity bound 1 h). Configs without the keys behave byte-identically.

the cloud providers in the same config keep the global watchdog untouched,
and the stall line names the override (`idle window 1800s (role default
override)`) so a wide window never reads as a hang.

capability hints).

## Provider queue

Project or user file section; the `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE` env var carries
the same JSON list and WINS over both files (issue #418). The ordered
failover chain replaces the main model: the first healthy entry serves,
a dead provider hands over loudly to the next, the winner sticks for
the session (RAM-only, never persisted), and cooled-down entries
re-enter rotation:

```yaml
providersQueue:
  - provider_type: openai-completions
    provider_config:
      model: moonshotai/Kimi-K2.6
      baseUrl: https://gate.example/v1
      apiKeyEnv: OPENAI_API_KEY
  - provider_type: anthropic
    provider_config:
      model: claude-sonnet-4-6
      apiKeyEnv: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
```

`apiKeyEnv` names the ENV indirection — a key VALUE never lives in the
yaml. CLI equivalent: `/providers queue list|add|remove|move|test`;
edits persist to the winning scope's file and go live from the next
turn. App Settings carries the same editor (env scope is read-only
there).

## Memory

<!-- parity: /memory -->

The long-term memory location. `memory:` may live in the user file or the
project file — project wins.

```yaml
memory:
  projectPath: ./memory        # inside the repo; committed with it
  userPath: ~/memory           # or a user-level store
```

neither edits paths; the section is the only way to set them. The live memory
controller re-reads the section (project resolution via `loadProjectMemoryConfig`),

## Tool availability

<!-- parity: /tools -->

`tools:` maps a tool id (or `mcp:<server>`) to on/off. Scopes, deepest wins
per key; the host's hard capability floor can never be overridden on:

1. global — `~/.fah/config.yaml` `tools:`
2. project — `<project>/.fah/config.yaml` `tools:`
3. session — `.tools/<sessionId>.yaml` next to the session file
4. runtime — `--tools` flag / `FA_TOOLS` env (this run only)

```yaml
tools:
  web_search: false
  mcp:
    fs: true                   # nested mcp: == mcp:<server> keys
```

CLI equivalent: `/tools enable|disable <id> [global|project|session]` writes
the matching scope file; `/tools` lists every id with its deciding scope;
`/tools reload` re-reads all scopes live. Disabled tools are hidden from the
model and tombstoned at execution. Edits apply live after a reload.

<!-- parity: /redact -->

    pii: true

## Compaction

Context-hiding engine choice (issue #148). User or project file (project
wins):

```yaml
compaction:
  engine: structured           # structured (default) | classic (rollback)
```

`structured` (the default since issue #287) hides records in place behind
one-line addressable markers (`compact_expand` restores any id or range
under a per-turn token budget); `classic` keeps the lossy summary
compaction — the legacy 1.0 rollback, selected through Settings →
Compaction (the app) or an explicit yaml/flag choice. Runtime override:
`fa --compaction-engine classic`; resolution is
flag > project > global > the structured default. Applies at
the next compaction.

<!-- parity: /skills -->

User file section governing third-party skill discovery
(`.claude/`, `.github/skills`, `.codex/`):

```yaml
skills:
  access: granted              # ask | granted | denied
  disableShellExecution: false # strip !`cmd` injections from third-party skills
```

## Approval

<!-- parity: /approval /allow -->

User file top-level keys:

```yaml
approvalMode: yolo             # always-ask | write | yolo | unattended
allowedTools:                  # always-allow list (exec tier still honors critical patterns per mode)
  - web_fetch
```

CLI equivalent: `/approval <mode>`, `/allow <tool>` — both persist to these
keys. Applies at next boot (the running session keeps its live mode).

## Power

User file section (issue #325, reworked in #326). Sleep prevention for
live runs — by default ONE assertion PER RUN (acquired when the run
goes in flight, released when it settles), so the machine cannot
idle/sleep out from under a long run but CAN sleep while the agent
idles between turns:

```yaml
power:
  sleepPrevention: idle # off | idle | display | system (default idle)
  hold: per-run # per-run | session (default per-run)
```

Levels are cumulative: `idle` keeps the system from idle-sleeping
(macOS `caffeinate -i`), `display` also keeps the display awake
(`-i -d`), `system` also blocks AC system sleep and declares the user
active (`-i -d -s -u`). `hold: session` is the explicit opt-in that
holds from session start to exit instead (always-on deployments).
macOS spawns `caffeinate -w <fa pid>` (exits with fa — never
orphaned), Linux tries `systemd-inhibit` best-effort, other platforms
no-op. A failed assertion is a warning, never a crash.

CLI equivalent: `/power` (level + hold + held state). Applies at next
boot.

## Subagents heartbeat

User file section (issue #383). While a background subagent runs, the
parent receives a periodic status digest through the steering channel —
age, provider requests/tokens, last activity, and a
`healthy | stalled | no-progress-since-spawn` classification per running
child. A child with no provider activity for `stallMinutes` (or that
never issued a request at all) gets a loud `⚠ STALLED` flag with the
suggested `task_status → task_cancel → respawn` action; the flag
escalates to `⚠⚠` at twice the threshold:

```yaml
subagents:
  heartbeatMinutes: 10 # digests cadence; 0 disables the heartbeat
  stallMinutes: 20 # quiet window before a stall flag; 0 disables flags
  replyAutoSpill: true # oversized child replies auto-spill to an artifact
```

Zero running children → no digest; completion notices are unchanged.
Config changes apply at the next digest tick — no restart required.

`subagents.replyAutoSpill` (gh-1956, default `true`): an oversized child
`reply` spills to an artifact automatically — the parent receives a bounded
excerpt + `agent://` pointer + completeness marker instead of raw bytes, and
manual chunking degrades to a fallback. Set it to `false` to restore the
pure-chunk behavior (the child must chunk long reports manually).

## Mode

<!-- parity: /mode /code /architect /review -->

User file top-level key:

```yaml
mode: code                     # code | architect | review
```

CLI equivalent: `/mode <name>` or the `/code`, `/architect`, `/review`

## Theme

<!-- parity: /theme -->

The TUI palette is data, never code. `/theme` lists every available theme
(built-ins first, then user themes) with a swatch preview; `/theme <name>`
switches immediately and persists the choice; `/theme reset` returns to
the default.

Config equivalent — the persisted theme name:

```yaml
tui:
  theme: default   # a built-in name or a user theme file stem
```

Built-in names: `default` (the historical site palette — teal `#5eead4`,
indigo `#818cf8`), `catppuccin`, `nord`, `dracula`, `ohmypi-dark`,
`ohmypi-light`, `pi`.

User themes live in `~/.fah/themes/<name>.json`; the file stem is the
theme name, and a user theme can never shadow a built-in (a clashing file
name is skipped with a boot note). The JSON holds a `"roles"` object mapping ROLE names to hex colors
(`"#rgb"` or `"#rrggbb"`): `accent`, `accent2`, `muted`, `highlight`,
`success`, `warning`, `error`, `border`, `focusBorder`, `userMessageBg`.
Every role is optional — a missing role inherits the default theme for
that slot. Unknown role names, invalid hex, or broken JSON produce a
named error (file, role, line) at load time, never a crash.

Applies: `/theme <name>` switches the live session in one frame; a direct
YAML edit takes effect at next boot. Asked to create a theme from a
description, write the JSON file, then apply it with `/theme <name>` and
confirm the swatch line with the user. Asked for a palette "like X" where
X is unknown, ask two or three palette questions first — never invent one
silently.

### Compaction report detail

By default an auto-compaction fold prints ONE short marker line
(`● auto-compacted · engine: N → M tokens (F freed · P%)`); the internal
checkpoint summary stays in the session file (reachable via
`compact_expand`) and out of the console. To render the full report block
(records + fenced summary) and the live summarizer stream on headless
runs, opt in:

```yaml
tui:
  showCompactionDetails: true
```

The manual `/compact` command always renders the full block. Applies at
next boot.

## Prompts, TTSR & A2A

The remaining user-file sections (all global scope):

```yaml
prompts:                        # prompt overrides: prompt id → text or @file
  concise: "Answer in one short paragraph."
ttsr:                           # tool-schema reduction (TTSR)
  enabled: true
  contextMode: keep             # keep | discard
  repeatMode: after-gap         # after-gap | once
a2a:                            # remote Agent2Agent endpoints

```

`a2a` servers are remote-only (a `url`, like remote MCP servers), so they
configure fine on process-less hosts. A `token` is an `\${ENV}` reference
resolved at boot; config `check`/`set` keep the token text literal, so an
unset variable surfaces when the agent boots, not as a config error.

## Output

<!-- parity: none (boot config only) -->

Console-output behavior flags (gh-1198 + gh-1433), user file. Today one
key — the live thinking stream for CLI line-mode runs: with
`streamThinking: true` (or the `--stream-thinking` flag, which wins for
the run), thinking deltas print dimmed and live like the TUI's, so ssh
sessions show the model's reasoning as it happens. The default `false`
keeps the interactive line-mode byte shape and prints a periodic
`… reasoning Ns` liveness line instead while a provider request sits
silent — the same waiting cadence the tool-liveness lines use
(`waiting.toolLivenessSeconds` / `toolLivenessTickSeconds`; `0` disables).

Since gh-1433 this key decides the INTERACTIVE faces only: a headless
`fa -p` run streams thinking and text by default (the log is the UI, no
flags needed). `--no-stream-thinking` silences thinking for one headless
run (the reasoning liveness line returns), and `FA_LOG_FIDELITY=legacy`
reverts the whole headless face to the pre-gh-1433 byte shape for edge
hosts that parse the log. Rendered deltas — thinking AND streamed text,
on every face — pass through the redaction pipeline at render time since
gh-1433: a registered secret echoed in a delta is masked live, so
byte-pin tests for interactive `--stream-thinking` sessions must assume
redacted deltas whenever redaction is enabled (default).

```yaml
output:
  streamThinking: false # interactive line mode only; headless runs stream by default
```

Applies at next boot (the flag applies to its own run).

## Tool-result & user-message spilling

<!-- parity: none (boot config only) -->

Oversized tool results spill to `.fah/spills/<sessionId>/<n>.txt` and
the session keeps a bounded preview + path + size stats (issue #678).
An oversized USER message (headless prompt, TUI input, steering) spills
to `.fah/spills/<sessionId>/user-<n>.md` and the model receives a
bounded head+tail preview plus a read-in-parts instruction (issue
#1760). Tolerant parse: unknown keys and mistyped scalars surface as
`[spills]` notes at boot, never boot failures. `enabled: false` = legacy
behavior (nothing spills — it beats the `FAH_SPILL_THRESHOLD` /
`FAH_USER_SPILL_THRESHOLD` env knobs too); `threshold: 0` disables
tool-result spilling only, `userThreshold: 0` the user path only:

```yaml
spills:
  enabled: true # kill switch; false = byte-identical legacy
  threshold: 8192 # chars above which a tool result spills; 0 = tools off
  headChars: 2000 # preview head bound (chars)
  tailChars: 2000 # preview tail bound (chars)
  userThreshold: 16384 # absolute byte floor for the user path; 0 = user off
  userFraction: 0.5 # spill a user message over this fraction of the live window budget
```

Applies at next boot.

## Session retention

<!-- parity: none (boot config only) -->

The `sessions:` section (gh-1746) is the opt-in disk hygiene policy for
the sessions root: when the total on disk crosses `maxTotalBytes`, a
boot sweep deletes whole session units oldest-last-used-first. Live
sessions (fresh heartbeats), named sessions, and sessions younger than
`minAgeDays` are always exempt — and with no `sessions:` section at all
nothing is EVER auto-deleted (byte-identical legacy boot). Tolerant
parse: unknown keys become notes, never boot failures. Run
`fa session clean [--dry-run]` to enforce the policy manually;
`sweep: off` makes the manual verb the only enforcement path:

```yaml
sessions:
  retention:
    maxTotalBytes: 5368709120 # total cap in bytes (0 = no cap, default)
    minAgeDays: 14 # never delete sessions used more recently than this
    keepNamed: true # named sessions (fa --session <name>) are exempt
    sweep: boot # boot (sweep at startup) | off (manual `fa session clean` only)
```

Applies at next boot (the sweep runs before the session opens).

## Project context budget

<!-- parity: notices on both surfaces; the byte knob is a config-file setting -->

`AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md`/`GEMINI.md`/`GOAL.md`/`DESIGN.md` + Copilot
instruction files merge into the system prompt under a byte budget,
allocated leaf-first (deeper files win, issue #1761). Truncation is never
silent: the model sees a head excerpt plus an explicit
read-the-full-file instruction, a dropped file leaves a one-line
tombstone, and the user gets a boot notice per truncated/dropped file.
Tolerant parse: unknown keys surface as `[projectContext]` notes at boot,
never boot failures. `maxBytes: 0` disables the section entirely (no file
reads, fast boot):

```yaml
projectContext:
  maxBytes: 32768 # merged budget; 0 = section off, no file reads
```

Applies at next boot.

The `links:` section (issue #691) is the single source of truth for

link changes in ONE place. Defaults are baked in; only overrides are
written. Strict parse: a non-map section, a non-URL value, or a

```yaml
links:
  appstore: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/fa-ai-agent/id6793815163

`play:` (the Google Play release) stays ABSENT until the Android release

`banner: false` is the regression switch: the Get surface stays

`tui:`/`fabric:`) and applies at next boot for the in-app banner; the

## Auto update

<!-- parity: /update, settings hub -->

User file top-level key (issue #1377). The self-update policy — a
tri-state, because the honest default is neither silent-off nor
unattended-on:

```yaml
auto_update: true # true | false | "notify" (default notify)
```

`notify` (the default) checks the release feed once at boot and prints
when a newer version exists — nothing is downloaded. `true` is the
unattended arm: at boot a newer release is downloaded, provenance
verified and installed, and the session restarts onto the new binary.
`false` touches no update host at all. An absent key and an explicit
`"notify"` are the same policy — the default is never written. Strict
parse: anything but `true`, `false` or `"notify"` is a
`ConfigException`. Applies at next boot. `/update` runs a check-and-apply
immediately regardless of the policy; the settings hub exposes the same
tri-state.

110:defaults by key: `memory`/`cube`/`tools` → the project file (created minimal
array or object) and it is rendered as a yaml block — `customProviders`
provider entries are settable this way, e.g. `config` op `set`, key
`customProviders`, value
`[{"name":"my-llama","apiType":"openai","baseUrl":"http://localhost:11434/v1","modelId":"llama3"}]`.
`get` reports list-valued keys as the same compact JSON, so the round
trip is get → edit the JSON → set. A whole list is replaced; to add one
entry, get first and re-set the extended list.
`get` of a platform-inapplicable key and `set` of one answer
`not applicable on this host` with the reason — never write there and
never suggest a file edit as a workaround. The stdio members of an MCP
server (`command`/`args`/`env`) need host process spawning: on web and
iOS/Android containers they are refused; configure a remote server via
`mcp.servers.<id>.url` instead. On a host with no home directory (web)
the global scope is refused for every user-file key — only the project
sections (`memory`/`cube`/`tools`) persist there.

python3 - <<'PYEOF'
# 1. _projectSections gains spills + the doc comments.
p = 'lib/src/config/config_service.dart'
s = open(p).read()
old = "const _projectSections = {'memory', 'cube', 'tools', 'compaction'};"
assert old in s
new = ("const _projectSections = {\n"
       "  'memory',\n"
       "  'cube',\n"
       "  'tools',\n"
       "  'compaction',\n"
       "  'spills',\n"
       "};")
s = s.replace(old, new, 1)
old9 = "/// file is read only for the `memory:`, `cube:` and `tools:` sections and"
assert old9 in s
s = s.replace(
    old9,
    "/// file is read only for the `memory:`, `cube:`, `tools:` and\n"
    "/// `spills:` sections and",
    1,
)
open(p, 'w').write(s)
print('config_service patched')

# 2. The CLI boot reads project spills (both wiring entry points).
p2 = 'lib/src/cli/agent_cli_spill.dart'
s2 = open(p2).read()
old2 = """  void attachSpillWiring() {
    final section = config.spills;"""
assert old2 in s2
new2 = """  void attachSpillWiring() {
    // gh-2411 rework review (spills): the PROJECT file participates in the
    // `spills:` section — resolve it exactly like the app host
    // (bin/fah_runapp.dart: loadProjectSpillsConfig(cwd) ?? saved.spills);
    // the self-settings doc already documents the project scope.
    final section = loadProjectSpillsConfig(_env.cwd) ?? config.spills;"""
s2 = s2.replace(old2, new2, 1)
old3 = """  void attachUserSpillWiring() {
    final section = config.spills;"""
assert old3 in s2
new3 = """  void attachUserSpillWiring() {
    final section = loadProjectSpillsConfig(_env.cwd) ?? config.spills;"""
s2 = s2.replace(old3, new3, 1)
open(p2, 'w').write(s2)
print('spill wiring patched')

# 3. The SKILL.md doc rows: scope defaults + the no-home-dir list.
p3 = 'prompts/skills/self-settings/SKILL.md'

    old4,
    "defaults by key: `memory`/`cube`/`tools`/`spills` → the project file (created minimal",
    1,
)
old5 = "sections (`memory`/`cube`/`tools`) persist there."
assert old5 in s3
s3 = s3.replace(
    old5,
    "sections (`memory`/`cube`/`tools`/`spills`) persist there.",
    1,
)
open(p3, 'w').write(s3)
print('SKILL.md patched')

The ticket folder input/ (PR diff, pr_discussions.md review threads, CI failures) IS your task: (1) answer EVERY open review thread in outputs/review_replies.json, (2) apply surgical code/test fixes on this PR's branch following TDD — modify ONLY the files and lines required to resolve open review threads, merge conflicts, or owned CI failures, and NEVER rewrite or refactor untouched/already-approved code in the PR, (3) push. A summary that claims the reds are "not caused by this PR" / "unrelated" / "infra" while owned violations are open is mechanically rejected: the leg fails and the no-op loop guard counts the lap.

# Reply — PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc68kjUd (soft-window warning wording)

**Agreed — the warning now states the actual regime condition.** Fixed in `87fc21f7c8`.

## The new wording

Your suggested shape, adapted to the code's numbers. `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_compaction.dart` (`_skipCompactionSoftWindow`) now computes the newest user turn's tokens the same way `softWindowRegime` does (`newestRealUserTurnIndex` + `estimateTokens`) and emits:

```
warning: context window 25000 cannot take a trim below its trigger — fixed
request overhead ≈21000 tokens + the newest user turn ≈6000 tokens already
reach it (estimated from the system prompt, tool schemas and the turn);
raising the window or disabling tools is the only fix; automatic compaction
is skipped while the context stays under the window
```

- The condition reported is the real one: `overhead + newestUserTurn >= window − reserve` (`windowBelowFixedOverhead`) — when a fat newest turn alone crossed the trigger, the warning no longer claims the overhead alone did it.
- The diagnostic line above it is untouched (already accurate, per your note) — this is only the user-facing wording, exactly as scoped.
- `docs/compaction.md`'s quote of the old text updated in the same commit so the doc stays truthful.
